objectives: Use the builder to design an array that passes the inverter's voltage, MPPT window and current checks
Calculate an array's DC/AC ratio and its design short-circuit current
Explain why a DC/AC ratio above 1, with a little clipping, usually pays

questions.prompt: Why do designers often connect more panel power than the inverter can pass, a DC/AC ratio above 1?
choices: Panels lose about half their rating in the wiring before the inverter
So the inverter can store the extra energy for the evening
Panels rarely reach full rating, so a smaller inverter runs nearer its rating and clips only a thin slice at noon
An inverter's AC rating is always higher than the DC power it takes in
questions.explain: Panels deliver their full rated power only in rare cool, bright moments. A slightly smaller inverter is cheaper and works nearer its rating for more hours; the price is clipping at midday on the sunniest days, a thin slice of the day's energy. An inverter does not store energy.

questions.prompt: Fourteen 430 W modules feed a 5 kW inverter. What is the DC/AC ratio?
questions.explain: The array is 14 × 0.43 kW = 6.02 kWp, and 6.02 ÷ 5 = 1.20. Dividing the other way round (5 ÷ 6.02 = 0.83) inverts the ratio, and the ratio uses the array's rating at standard test conditions, before any losses are taken off.

questions.prompt: When does a string come closest to the inverter's maximum voltage?
choices: At noon on a hot summer day, when the light is strongest
Late on a hot afternoon, when the modules are warmest
Whenever the inverter is clipping power at midday
On a bright, freezing morning, before current flows and the modules warm up
questions.explain: Silicon's voltage rises as it cools, about 0.27 % per °C, and the open-circuit voltage is highest when no current flows. So the risk peaks at sunrise on the coldest day. Hot afternoons do the opposite: the voltage drops, which can push a string below the MPPT window.

questions.prompt: An array has three strings in parallel, built from modules with a short-circuit current of 13.2 A. With the builder's 25 % safety margin, what design current must the inverter input accept?
questions.explain: Strings in parallel add their currents: 3 × 13.2 A = 39.6 A, and the builder adds 25 % for moments brighter than the rating: 39.6 × 1.25 = 49.5 A. 16.5 A is the margin on one string only, and 13.2 A forgets that parallel strings add current.
